_comment: Per-plate assessment of whether the tracked tables can faithfully redraw each stored corpus plate. Produced by agents that opened the stored image, its caption and the candidate tables, and checked plotted values against the data. REDRAWABLE requires every panel to be present.

E11_rem_a03_codes_by_era.evidence: E11 table: columns Code, Indicator, Definition era, 2019..2025; every cell is 'count (n establishments)' or 'outside the era'. Panels a/b/e/f read straight off it — 03500404 2019 = '37,952 (701)' matches the plate's first blue bar and its n=701; 09600212 2023 = '8,221 (731)' matches the plate label '8,221 (n=731)'; 03700104 2024 = '39,466 (694)' matches panel f. Panel d's two ratio rows are present verbatim: '62.8% (60.9–64.6)' all months and '39.2% (36.8–41.6)' excluding Feb 2019. Panel c is MONTHLY and is not in the E11 table; I found it in output_files/consolidacion/rem_monthly_region_raw_columns.csv (year, Mes, IdRegion, CodigoPrestacion, Col01..Col50). Summing Col01+Col02 over regions for 2019 reproduces the annual totals EXACTLY (03500404 37,952; 03500405 5,160; 03500406 2,613; 03500407 1,640) and the February 2019 outlier the caption names (03500406 = 1,051, 03500407 = 1,028). The 12 monthly values per code (716/1,189/2,072/... for 03500404) track the plate's log-scale lines. The 'excluding February' numerator/denominator the plate prints (612/1,562) = 1,640−1,028 and 2,613−1,051, both recoverable.
E11_rem_a03_codes_by_era.estimator_note: Unweighted administrative counts, never survey estimates; no weighting applies. Series A annual FLOW = sum of months of COL01+COL02 for A03 (confirmed: Col01-only gives 19,279 for 03500404 in 2019, which does NOT match the plate's 37,952 — Col01+Col02 does). Counts, not rates; no standardisation anywhere. Panel d is a within-code-year proportion with Wilson limits (recomputable). The tracked E11 table matches the stored plate value for value; the monthly file is a different lineage (2017–2024) but its 2019 annual sums equal the E11 table exactly, so the two are consistent.
E11_rem_a03_codes_by_era.labels_note: The stored plate is in ENGLISH, not Spanish — as are all ten of these plates, captions.json, titles.json and plates.qmd (grep for 'Región', 'establecimientos', 'autismo', 'según', 'Tasa' over captions.json returns 0 hits). No translation layer is needed and none should be invented. Panels a/b legend strings ('Health control at 18 months', 'Language and/or social-area alteration at the control', 'M-CHAT performed (children with an alteration)', 'M-CHAT altered (children with an alteration)') are VERBATIM in the table's Indicator column. Panels e/f use short y-tick forms ('Suspected elsewhere', 'Low risk', 'High with referral', 'Part 2: medium in part 1', 'Alert: yes', 'Motive: EEDP', '30–59 mo referral') that are NOT verbatim anywhere tracked — the drawing code must supply a code→short-label map, or fall back to the table's long names. The only Spanish tracked for these series is the raw REM code wording in output_files/consolidacion/rem_annual_by_code.csv ('TRASTORNO GENERALIZADOS DEL DESARROLLO'), which would be wrong to print on this plate.

E12_rem_a03_risk_referral.estimator_note: Unweighted administrative counts (annual flow, sum of months); no survey weighting. E13_rem_a05_regional.evidence: E13 table cells are 'count / rate (n)', e.g. Ñuble 2023 = '899 / 173.1 (47)'. Panel a (rate heatmap) and panel b (establishment heatmap) come straight off it — Arica 2021 = 15.7 and n=10; Metropolitana 2022 n=157; both match the plate. Panel c: I recomputed the Spearman ρ of each year's 16 regional rates against 2021 and got 0.721, 0.738, 0.759, 0.385 — the plate prints '2022: 0.72; 2023: 0.74; 2024: 0.76; 2025: 0.39', and the 2025 rank order from the same rates is Ñuble 1, Magallanes 2, Aysén 3, Biobío 4, exactly the plate's right-hand legend. Panel f: median/IQR/min–max of those rates give 2025 median 85.1, min 29.9, max 208.8 and the plate's grey max labels 45 / 97 / 173 / 171 / 209 — all match, with the national line at 65.1 from the 'Chile (national total)' row. Panel d: the E13 table has ONLY a '% of entries contributed by the stable panel (2025)' column — one point per region. S6_stable_panel.csv supplies the national red line (73.0, 61.5, 52.0, 48.1, 51.4, exactly the plate's labels) but is national-only. The 16 grey region lines for 2021–2024 (64 values) exist nowhere tracked; output_files/consolidacion/rem_establishment_panel.csv has establishment-level rows but stops at 2024, so the 258-establishment stable set (which requires presence in every year 2021–2025) cannot even be defined. Panel e: plots the VARIANT PDD FAMILY regional rate for 2025, not strict autism — its n values differ from the table's strict n (plate Metropolitana n=246 vs strict 227; Biobío 163 vs 161; Maule 88 vs 82) and its national reference is 77.5, which I found only as a NATIONAL figure in S7_a05_standardised_rates.csv ('PDD family ... 2025 ... 15,670 ... 77.5 (76.3 to 78.8) ... 995'). No tracked table holds A05 family counts by region for 2025: output_files/consolidacion/rem_rates_regional.csv carries only series 05990022/05990027 and ends at 2024, and rem_a05_region_age_sex.csv likewise ends at 2024.
E13_rem_a05_regional.estimator_note: Unweighted administrative counts; no survey weighting. Panels a/e are CRUDE ecological rates per 100,000 (REM locates the provider, not residence) — NOT standardised; the standardised A05 series lives separately in S7/S_a05_standardised_rates.csv and must not be substituted. Panel b is a count of establishments. Panel c is a rank/Spearman derived statistic. Panel e uses exact Poisson limits on the family count. The stored E13 table matches the plate for panels a/b/c/f and gives pre-computed rates, so no population denominator is needed for those.
E13_rem_a05_regional.labels_note: English plate. Region names are verbatim in the table's Region column (Spanish place names: 'Ñuble', 'Valparaíso', "O'Higgins", 'La Araucanía', 'Arica y Parinacota'), so panels a/b/e/f need no invented labels. Panel c prints abbreviated names ('Arica y P.', 'Antofag.', 'Metropol.', 'Araucanía') that are not tracked — the code must abbreviate. Panel titles and axis strings are English and must be authored.
blockers: Panel (d): the stable-panel share by REGION for 2021–2025 is not tracked. E13 carries only the 2025 column (16 points); S6_stable_panel.csv and E72/ST3 are national or module-level only. rem_establishment_panel.csv ends at 2024, so the stable-panel membership set cannot be rebuilt either. 16 of the panel's 17 series are unavailable.

Panel (e): regional variant-PDD-family A05 rates for 2025 with exact Poisson limits and family establishment counts are not tracked. rem_rates_regional.csv holds only the strict code 05990022 (and 05990027) and stops at 2024; rem_a05_region_age_sex.csv stops at 2024. Only the national family reference line (77.5) is recoverable, from S7_a05_standardised_rates.csv.
Do NOT substitute the strict-autism regional rates of panel (a) for panel (e) — the plate's own n values prove they are different denominators of establishments and different counts.

Family minus strict per age group gives +289, +702, +688, +470, +132, +67, +55, +29, +17, +19, +13, +11, +6, +8, +3, +3, +2 — every one of the plate's 17 green difference labels, and the family n=995 in E70's brackets matches the plate legend.
E14_rem_a05_age_sex.estimator_note: Unweighted administrative counts (annual flow; age x sex cells COL04–COL37). Panel c carries BOTH estimators and they must not be confused: dashed = CRUDE rate per 100,000 against INE residents; square markers = age-STANDARDISED to the WHO standard with Fay–Feuer limits. Both are pre-computed in the E14 table, so no denominator or standard population file is needed. Panel d is a ratio of RECORDS with exact limits, not a ratio of rates. Panel f is counts, not rates. The tracked table matches the stored plate exactly; E70 is the plate's own extended companion and its strict-autism rows equal E14's counts.
E14_rem_a05_age_sex.labels_note: English plate. Age-group labels '0–4' … '80+' are verbatim in the table's first column and in E70's 'Age group' column. 'Males'/'Females' are verbatim in the Series/Sex columns. 'Strict autism' / 'PDD family (variant)' in panel f are short forms of E70's Category strings ('Autism (single code)' / 'Variant PDD family (sum of codes)') — the code supplies the shortening. Caution: docs/study/data/rem_a05_age_sex_annual.csv and output_files/consolidacion/rem_a05_region_age_sex.csv carry SPANISH sex labels ('Hombres'/'Mujeres', 'HOMBRE'/'MUJER'); those must not be printed on this English plate. Use S8_a05_age_sex.csv only with care — it collapses 50+ into a single group and cannot draw panel f's last seven bars.

E15_rem_p2_p6_detail.evidence: Panel a is a region x year heatmap of the P2 December rate. CRITICAL FINDING: E73's regional INE rows are exactly DOUBLE the true population — the 16 regions sum to 38,214,432 against a national 19,107,216 in 2019 (ratio 2.000 in every year), and S9 gives Arica 2024 = 261,779 against E73's 523,558. Using E73/2 I reproduced the ENTIRE panel-a matrix cell for cell: 13.8 15.9 14.1 38.4 57.4 91.7 191.9 for Arica, 27.6 28.3 52.7 87.6 154.6 203.2 219.3 for Ñuble, 2.8 <5 <5 9.9 43.4 87.9 101.5 for Magallanes — identical to the plate, suppressed cells included. Panels b/c/d/e all come from E15 alone: December and June with n for P2 (1,854 (460) … 29,974 (1,325); June 1,502 (374) … 26,195 (1,256)), the n rows below panel b (460/400/640/897/1,012/1,218/1,325 blue, 482/704/956/1,160/1,274 green, 95/113/129/144/153 orange) all present; panel c is value/n and I checked 12,645/153 = 82.6 and 6,624/111 = 59.7 against the plate's orange line; panel d's NANEAS row (59,907 (1,187) / 77,081 (1,293) / 100,789 (1,394)) and its Wilson row (22.0% (21.7–22.4), 28.2%, 29.7%) match the printed diamonds; panel e's four family/strict series and the legend n ranges (482–1,274; 95–153; 815–1,344; 132–169) are all in the table. Panel f is the failure: it is a regional dumbbell of P6 STRICT codes, labelled 'Primary care (P6241010)' and 'Specialty (P6241060)' on the plate, but E71's 2021–2025 P6 blocks are the VARIANT F84 FAMILY (national totals 27,319 / 20,365, which equal E15's family rows, not its strict rows 21,843 / 12,645). Checked numerically: Ñuble family primary 2025 = 2,178 over pop 523,876 gives 415.7, while the plate prints 404; family specialty 1,120 gives 213.8 against the plate's 173. The plate's per-region n pairs also differ from E71's family n (Ñuble 57/5 vs 60/5; Biobío 169/10 vs 178/16; Metropolitana 227/45 vs 244/55).
E15_rem_p2_p6_detail.estimator_note: Unweighted administrative counts; no survey weighting. Series P is a semester STOCK, not a flow — December is the main measure, June the sensitivity, and the two are never summed. Panel a is a CRUDE ecological rate per 100,000 (provider region, not residence); panel c is a per-establishment ratio, not a rate; panel d is a within-code-year Wilson proportion. The E15 table matches the plate exactly for panels b–e. E71 matches the plate for the P2 block (panel a) but is the FAMILY definition, not strict, for the P6 blocks — a straight name-match on E71 would silently put family values under strict-code labels.
E15_rem_p2_p6_detail.labels_note: English plate. Region names verbatim in E71's 'Region of the establishment' column and in E73's Category column (they agree: 'Ñuble', 'Valparaíso', "O'Higgins", 'La Araucanía'). Series names 'P2 ASD', 'P6 primary care', 'P6 specialty', 'Broad PDD (pre-2021)', 'Strict autism', 'PDD family (variant)' are all present in E15's Series column, though as compounds ('P6 primary care — Broad PDD (pre-2021)') that the code must split for the legends. No Spanish rendering exists or is needed.
blockers: Panel (f): the P6 STRICT codes (P6241010 primary, P6241060 specialty) by region for 2025, with their per-region establishment counts, are not tracked. E71's 2021–2025 P6 blocks are the variant F84 family, verified by its national totals matching E15's family rows and by the plate's own n pairs and rates disagreeing with the family values. Both of the panel's series are unavailable.

Redraw trap for panel (a): E73_denominator_layers_full.csv's regional INE rows are exactly 2x the true population (regions sum to twice the stated national total in every year). The drawing code must halve them, or every regional rate on this plate — and on any other plate built on that column — comes out at half the published value.

Panels a–e are counts; only panel f is a rate, and it is CRUDE and ecological, not standardised. Use E73's NATIONAL row here — the regional rows in that file are doubled (see E15) but are not needed for this plate. The tracked table is the plate's own companion and matches it value for value.
E16_rem_a27_a28_regional.labels_note: English plate and the cleanest label match of the ten. The legend strings 'Counselling (29101566)', 'Assisted referral (29101574)', 'Primary rehabilitation (29101629)', 'Hospital rehabilitation (29101651)' are VERBATIM in the table's Series column, and all sixteen region names are verbatim in its Region column. E17_rem_establishment_distribution.evidence: The E17 table holds only SUMMARY statistics per indicator-year: Reporting establishments, Gini, % contributed by the top decile, median 'Value per establishment', and six threshold counts. Panel d is fully in it — A05 strict Gini 0.59/0.60/0.61/0.60/0.61 and top decile 48.9/46.4/46.3/43.1/44.4, P2 38.0 and 39.9 at 2019–2020, all matching the plate's lines. Panel e is fully in it — A05 2025 bars 952/553/376/163/51/6 and the 2021 hollow markers 449/115/44/12/3/2, P2 2025 1,325/876/649/371/184/46 against 2019 460/122/55/3/0/0, P6 primary 2025 1,273/756/537/290/110/25 against 2021 475/142/59/10/0/0 — every bar and marker on the plate. Panels a, b and c are LORENZ CURVES and panel f is a box-with-outliers: all four need the full per-establishment value distribution, which summary statistics cannot give. The only establishment-level file tracked is output_files/consolidacion/rem_establishment_panel.csv (year, code, IdEstablecimiento, Col01). It is genuine — for code 05990022 it reproduces n = 449/658/920/1,070, totals 2,085/4,640/8,049/11,842, Gini 0.59/0.60/0.61/0.60, medians 2/3/4/5 and the threshold counts 115/44/12/3/2 and 574/376/124/32/3 exactly. But it stops at 2024, so the 2025 curve of panel a and the 2025 box of panel f cannot be drawn, and it contains ONLY Serie A codes (03500404…, 05990022–31, 09600212–19, 29101629, 29101651) — no P2500500 and no P6241010, so panels b and c have no source at all. I confirmed by grep that rem_establishment_panel.csv is the only file anywhere tracked with an establishment identifier column.
E17_rem_establishment_distribution.estimator_note: Unweighted administrative counts per establishment-year; no survey weighting. Values are an annual FLOW for A05 and a December STOCK for P2/P6 — the plate keeps them in separate panels and they must never share an axis. Gini and top-decile share are concentration measures of administrative reporting, not of people with autism. Establishments with a row but a zero value stay in the Gini and threshold calculations; establishments with no row are not zeros. The E17 table matches the plate for panels d and e; the establishment panel is a consistent but shorter-running lineage (2017–2024) whose recomputed statistics agree with E17 to within rounding (top decile differs by 0.4pp in 2021–2022 because of the decile cut rule).
E17_rem_establishment_distribution.labels_note: English plate. The indicator names on the plate ('A05 strict autism (entries)', 'P2 ASD (December)', 'P6 primary care (December)', 'P6 specialty (December)') and the threshold tick labels ('≥ 1' … '≥ 100') are VERBATIM in the table's Series and Value columns, so panels d and e need no invented strings. Panel titles are English and authored. No Spanish rendering exists or is needed.
blockers: Panels (b) and (c): Lorenz curves for P2 ASD December and P6 primary-care December need per-establishment values for Serie P codes. No tracked file holds any establishment-level Serie P data — rem_establishment_panel.csv covers Serie A codes only. Zero of these panels' curves (7 and 5 respectively) are drawable.
Panel (a): 4 of the 5 Lorenz curves (2021–2024) are drawable from rem_establishment_panel.csv, but 2025 is not — that file ends at 2024.

Panel (f): 4 of the 5 boxes (2021–2024) are drawable; the 2025 box, its whiskers and its outliers are not. The E17 table supplies only the median (the plate's 'med=' labels), never the quartiles, whiskers or individual points.
Do not fake a Lorenz curve from the Gini or the threshold counts — they determine neither the curve's shape nor the outliers.
